original_title: Diastereo- and Enantioselective Synthesis of 9-Aryl-1-vinyl-tetrahydro-β-carbolines via Brønsted Acid-Catalyzed Pictet–Spengler Reaction
title: Locking down the axial chirality in vinyl tetrahydro-β-carbolines
blurb: A Brønsted acid-catalyzed Pictet-Spengler on N-indole-tethered allenamides builds 9-aryl-1-vinyl-tetrahydro-β-carbolines with better than 20:1 dr, and swapping in a chiral phosphoric acid sets the C-N axial chirality up to 98% ee. It needs an ortho-amide directing group to hold that stereocontrol together, but the vinyl handle left dangling on the product is what makes it useful past this paper.

original_title: Modular assembly of bioisosteric bridged aza-frameworks via ring strain release
title: Breaking strained rings to make azetidine bioisosteres
blurb: A strained azatricycloalkane platform undergoes stereocontrolled C-N bond cleavage to deliver a spread of azabicyclo[x.1.1]alkanes built as drop-in bioisosteres. They back it up with real targets, orexin receptor antagonists and azetidine replacements, instead of just cataloguing the ring system.

original_title: 25 Phase II Trial of Sacituzumab Tirumotecan in Patients with SMARCB1-Deficient Renal Medullary Carcinoma Previously Treated with at Least One Prior Line of Therapy: STaRMC Trial (NCT07438626)
title: A TROP2 ADC gets its shot at a cancer nobody else wants to treat
blurb: STaRMC is a Phase II trial of sacituzumab tirumotecan in SMARCB1-deficient renal medullary carcinoma, a brutal RCC that mostly hits young people with sickle hemoglobinopathies and shrugs off anti-angiogenics, mTOR inhibitors, and immunotherapy alike. Median survival's been stuck around two years, so a TROP2-directed ADC for patients past one prior line is at least a new lever. This is the trial design, not results yet.

original_title: EDA-Driven Radical Relay Strategy for the Strain-Release Functionalization of Bicyclobutanes
title: Light and a bit of SO2 turn bicyclobutanes into spirocyclic sulfones
blurb: No catalyst, just visible light and an in-situ electron donor-acceptor complex driving radical sulfonylation of bicyclobutanes, cyclizing, grabbing SO2, and springing the strained ring open in one cascade to give lactam-spirocyclobutyl oxindole sulfones. They actually ran the mechanistic case, UV-vis, fluorescence quenching, a Job's plot, EPR, rather than just asserting the EDA complex is there.

original_title: Light-Triggered Decoding of Hydrophobic Interactions in Living Systems
title: Turning the hydrophobic effect on and off with light, inside living cells
blurb: Hydrophobicity is normally baked into a carbon skeleton and impossible to touch on the fly. This encodes it into water-soluble charged radical precursors and decodes it back out with visible light under physiological conditions, giving spatiotemporal control over an effect that usually just runs quietly in the background of membrane assembly and protein folding.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Sustainable Oxidation of Sulfides to Sulfoxides: Recent Advances in Catalyst Design and Oxygen‐Transfer Control (2021–2026)
title: Five years of trying to stop sulfoxides from becoming sulfones
blurb: A 2021-2026 review of sulfide oxidation catalysts framed around the actual hard part, controlling oxygen transfer precisely enough to stop at the sulfoxide instead of overshooting, while still tolerating real functional groups. Less about which oxidant is fashionable, more about who's actually cracked the selectivity problem.

original_title: Pd-Catalyzed Asymmetric Bicyclization/Cyanation of Propargylic Esters-Alkenes: Construction of Chiral Aza[3.1.0]bicycles Containing Alkenyl Nitriles
title: A one-pot Pd cascade builds chiral aza-bicycles with a nitrile tail
blurb: Propargylic ester-tethered 1,6-enynes run through oxidative addition, isomerization, bicyclization, and cyanation in one palladium-catalyzed cascade, with Zn(CN)2 as the cyanide source. Out come chiral aza[3.1.0]bicycles carrying an alkenyl nitrile, in good yield and with the outstanding selectivity you'd want from something billed as asymmetric.

original_title: Spirooxindole Derivatives as Emerging Scaffolds in Drug Discovery: Synthetic Strategies, Structure–Activity Relationship, and Biological Activities
title: A round-up of how people are building spirooxindoles now
blurb: A review tallying the current synthetic routes to spirooxindoles, multicomponent 1,3-dipolar cycloadditions, organocatalytic cascades, one-pot protocols, and the pyrrolidine, cyclopropyl carboxamide, carbamate, oxadiazoline, pyrrolizidine, and furan derivatives that keep coming out submicromolar to low-micromolar in cytotoxicity assays. A scaffold catalog more than a new finding.

original_title: Rapid Photogelation of Low‐Concentration Polymer Solutions via Photodimerization of o ‐Ethylnitrobenzene
title: A UV crosslinker that gels dilute PVA in half a second
blurb: o-Ethylnitrobenzene grafted onto poly(vinyl alcohol) photodimerizes under UV and turns a dilute (~0.5 wt%) aqueous solution into a flexible, elastic hydrogel in about half a second. Compressive resilience holds up too.

original_title: Carbene-Catalyzed Divergent Synthesis of Cyclic Imidic Acid Derivatives via Dehydrogenative Coupling
title: Carbene catalysis takes cyclic imidic acid synthesis past just amides
blurb: Cross-dehydrogenative coupling of cyclic aldimines had only ever been worked out for amine partners, giving amides. A carbene catalyst opens the same coupling to alcohols and thiols as well, so one method now reaches amides, imidates, and thioimidates instead of amides being the only door in.

original_title: Modular Assembly of Unsymmetric 3,4-Dihydro-BINAP Derivatives via Electrophilic Phosphinative Cyclization of Alkynes and Sequential C–P Cross-Coupling
title: Building unsymmetric BINAP-type ligands module by module
blurb: A Tf2O-promoted phosphination/cyclization cascade fuses a diarylphosphine oxide onto a naphthyl alkyne to assemble the 3,4-dihydronaphthyl and phosphine pieces together, then a nickel-catalyzed C-P coupling bolts on the second naphthyl unit. Four tunable modules snapped together in sequence, aimed at unsymmetric variants that plain BINAP synthesis doesn't give you.

original_title: Design of a spermine-β-cyclodextrin functionalized gelatin nanoaggregate hydrogel for nose-to-brain delivery of donepezil.
title: A cyclodextrin-decked gelatin gel aimed at getting donepezil past the nose
blurb: Spermine and β-cyclodextrin hung off a gelatin nanoaggregate hydrogel, built for nose-to-brain donepezil delivery. Reads as a formulation and design piece, the kind where whether it actually gets the drug where it's supposed to go is still an open question.

original_title: Submolecular video-imaging of the Smc5/6 complex topologically bound to DNA
title: Watching Smc5/6 grip DNA one domain at a time
blurb: High-speed AFM resolves individual domains of the Smc5/6 complex sitting on DNA. The ATP-bound complex holds on via its ATPase head, but once ATP is hydrolyzed the DNA gets pulled inside the SMC ring itself. A direct, submolecular look at a mechanism people had mostly inferred before.

original_title: Electrochemical Phase Formation of electroactive and nanostructured PbO2 from Acetate Media: Insights into Nucleation, Growth, and Interfacial Mechanisms
title: Mapping how PbO2 nucleates out of an acetate bath
blurb: Cyclic voltammetry, potentiostatic current transients, SEM, and EDX track PbO2 forming on glassy carbon from acetate media, with new redox features tracking the oxide film as it takes over the electrode. Growth follows the standard progressive two-dimensional nucleation pattern, solid mechanistic bookkeeping rather than a surprise.

original_title: Understanding In-Liquid Sample Environments for Infrared Nanospectroscopy of Soft Materials
title: What that membrane does to your IR nanospectroscopy signal
blurb: s-SNOM IR nanospectroscopy on wet samples works by sandwiching an ultrathin membrane between the AFM tip and the liquid, letting the evanescent field through without the tip ever touching liquid. This works out how that membrane itself shapes the near- and far-field response, since it's part of the optical stack whether you account for it or not.

original_title: Synthesis of Pyrrolidinyl PNA and Its Site-Specific Labeling at Internal Positions by Click Chemistry.
title: Building pyrrolidinyl PNA with a click handle inside the chain
blurb: A methods chapter on synthesizing pyrrolidinyl PNA and site-specifically labeling it at internal positions using click chemistry. A protocol, not a result.

original_title: Zn-Promoted Radical Azo-Coupling: A Halogen-Atom-Transfer-Promoted C(sp3)–N Formation
title: Zinc turns diazonium salts into a radical relay for C(sp3)-N bonds
blurb: Zn hands an electron to aryl diazonium salts to make aryl radicals, which grab a halogen off alkyl iodides to make alkyl radicals, which then couple onto azo. No precious metal anywhere in that chain. The nice bit is substrates set up for 1,5-HAT skip straight to C-H functionalized products, so the radical does extra work for free.

original_title: Prognostic value of circulating tumor DNA and copy-number alterations in patients receiving tandem [(225)Ac]Ac-/[(177)Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 therapy for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer: a prospective observational study.
title: ctDNA and copy-number changes as a readout for tandem Ac-225/Lu-177 PSMA therapy
blurb: A prospective study tracking circulating tumor DNA and copy-number alterations in mCRPC patients getting tandem Ac-225/Lu-177-PSMA-617, to see if either predicts who actually benefits. Useful if it pans out, since picking responders up front beats finding out after a round of alpha therapy.

original_title: Defect Engineering on Amorphous NiFeB Alloys for the Selective Conversion of KA Oil Into Adipic Acid
title: Amorphous NiFeB alloy pushes KA oil electro-oxidation toward adipic acid
blurb: Screening Ni-Fe/Cr/Mn LDHs and their boronized, amorphized versions for turning KA oil into adipic acid electrochemically, the Ni4Fe1B alloy came out on top: 581.5 mA/cm² normalized current density and 52.7% adipic acid selectivity at 1.6 V. They're crediting defects from the amorphization for the boost. Decent numbers, but 52.7% selectivity means almost half the product is still going somewhere else.

original_title: Three-Component Radical C–H Selenylation of N -Acyl Anilines under Metal-Free Conditions
title: Elemental selenium powder does C-H selenylation, no metal needed
blurb: A three-component, bromide-catalyzed reaction that arylselenylates N-acyl anilines straight from Se powder and boronic acids, skipping the toxic, unstable selenyl reagents that usually make this chemistry a pain to run. Broad boronic acid scope including the sterically awkward ones, and it's metal-free to boot.

original_title: Cu(OTf)2-Catalyzed Insertion of Unactivated Alkynes into C–F Bonds of Benzyl Fluorides
title: Cu(OTf)2 turns benzylic C-F bonds into alkenyl fluorides via alkyne insertion
blurb: Copper triflate inserts unactivated alkynes right into the C-F bond of benzyl fluorides, giving stereodefined alkenyl fluorides, and it picks out C-F over C-Cl and C-Br in the same molecule. Mechanistic work points to benzyl and alkenyl cation intermediates carrying the reaction. Selective C-F activation is the rare kind, since C-F bonds are usually the ones everyone avoids touching.

original_title: Nickel-Catalyzed Reductive Amination of Aldehydes and Nitroarenes
title: Nickel does reductive amination straight from nitroarenes
blurb: A Ni-catalyzed route that couples aldehydes with nitro(hetero)arenes to make secondary amines in one step, no need to pre-reduce the nitro group first. High yields across aromatic, aliphatic, and heterocyclic partners, with the aliphatic-aldehyde cases pulling in functional groups that matter for drug and agrochemical synthesis.

original_title: Competition between Photoinduced Electron Transfer and Heterolytic Cleavage on Boron in B-Phenoxy Substituted BODIPY Photocages
title: BODIPY photocages leak electrons instead of just cleaving cleanly
blurb: B-phenoxy BODIPY photocages were supposed to release phenol on light, but tuning the para substituent from strong to weak electron-withdrawing barely moved the needle, quantum yields stayed pinned at 0.01-0.03 across the board. TD-DFT points to photoinduced electron transfer competing with the heterolytic cleavage you actually want, which is a bad sign if you were hoping to dial in efficiency by picking substituents.

original_title: Computational prediction of substrate scope of a homogeneous catalyst: the case of metal-free C–H borylation by a frustrated Lewis pair catalyst
title: Predicting FLP borylation scope from first principles, not just the fast pathway
blurb: A computational approach to substrate scope for metal-free C-H borylation with a frustrated Lewis pair catalyst that bothers to model the competing, turnover-killing pathways alongside the favored one, not just the lowest-energy route. That's the part worth noting, since most scope predictions quietly assume the shortcut.

original_title: Controlling Structures and Properties of NaCl‐Containing Alginate/Polyacrylamide Tough Hydrogels via a One‐Pot Process
title: Salt goes into the hydrogel from the start instead of soaking in later
blurb: Alginate/polyacrylamide tough hydrogels usually get their NaCl by soaking, which takes a while and leaves concentration gradients baked in. This one-pot version puts the salt in during synthesis instead, aimed at more uniform structure for the strain-sensor and wearable-electronics crowd.

original_title: Ammonia Diverts Ozonolysis from C═C Scission to Nitrogen Incorporation via Competitive Adsorption and Nucleophilic Trapping
title: Ammonia hijacks ozone before it can cut squalene's double bonds
blurb: Ozonolysis of squalene normally scissions the C=C bonds, but gaseous ammonia cuts ozone uptake threefold by competing for the same reactive sites, and NH3·H2O complexes then trap the Criegee intermediate to shove nitrogen into the product instead of cleaving the chain. DFT and kinetic modeling back up the competitive-adsorption story. A reminder that ambient NH3 isn't just a bystander in atmospheric ozone chemistry, it's actively rerouting it.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: 1,2-Sulfonylalkynylation of Alkynes to Access Sulfonyl-Substituted 1,3-Enyne Compounds via Nickel/Photoredox Dual Catalysis
title: A nickel/photoredox combo builds tetrasubstituted sulfonyl enynes
blurb: Photoredox/nickel dual catalysis couples alkynes with sodium sulfinates and bromoalkynes in a redox-neutral, three-component reaction, delivering sulfonyl 1,3-enynes with excellent E-selectivity. The notable bit: internal alkynes play along too, giving tetrasubstituted enynes that are usually a pain to make.

original_title: Recent Advances in Photochemical and Photoelectrochemical Fluoroalkylation: Direct Use of Fluoroalkyl Carboxylic Acids
title: Fluoroalkylation without the usual finicky reagents
blurb: A review rounding up photochemical and photoelectrochemical methods that install fluoroalkyl groups straight from fluoroalkyl carboxylic acids, skipping the expensive, unstable reagents and stoichiometric oxidants most protocols still lean on. Survey piece, not new chemistry, but a useful map of where the field's landed.

original_title: Synthesis of Stereodivergent Chirally Pure Acyclic Polyols Based Quinone–Triazole Glycohybrids as Privileged Scaffolds
title: Quinones get a chirally pure polyol makeover
blurb: A one-pot, stereodivergent route grafts triazole-linked polyol chains onto quinone scaffolds by way of azido-dideoxy glycol addition and intramolecular cycloaddition, aiming at the solubility and off-target toxicity problems that keep quinones out of the clinic despite being a favorite redox-active core.

original_title: Self‐Feeding Living Materials Enabled by Cell Responsive Glycogen Nanoparticles as Metabolic Batteries
title: Glycogen crumbs keep engineered tissue alive when the blood supply can't reach it
blurb: Scaling living materials past a few millimeters usually starves the core of oxygen and nutrients. Feeding cells extracellular glycogen nanoparticles instead lets human mesenchymal stromal cells survive weeks of anoxia and serum deprivation, and apparently they secrete their own glycogen-degrading enzymes to tap it, which contradicts what the field assumed about these cells.

original_title: Topological Control of Carbon Nanohoops for Boosted Long-Range Coherent Transport
title: Loop your nanohoop twice, get better conductance
blurb: Double-loop carbon nanohoop junctions, built from conjoined bisnanohoops with 15-plus phenylene units, show higher conductance and a much shallower drop-off with length than single-loop or linear versions of the same size. The asymmetric curvature between the two loops is what steers the gold contacts into that double-loop geometry in the first place.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Creating bottom-up RNA transfer vehicles from synthetic protein assemblies
title: AI-designed virus-like shells outperform actual viruses at RNA delivery
blurb: Synthetic virus-like protein capsids designed by AI beat their naturally evolved counterparts at getting RNA into cells. The argument is that real viruses evolved under constraints like immune evasion and replication, not payload delivery, so a from-scratch design can just skip all that baggage.

original_title: Catalytic Regulation of Cluster-Mediated Growth Enables Scalable Synthesis of Shape-Controlled Single-Crystalline Silver Nanocrystals
title: Dialing in silver nanocrystal shape with a copper assist
blurb: A copper-assisted, one-pot heating process steers cluster-mediated growth of silver nanocrystals into uniform, single-crystalline particles, tunable from 5 to 11 nm and shaped anywhere from truncated-octahedral to spherical. Getting that much shape control on single-crystal Ag at scale is normally the hard part.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Promiscuous Monocopper(II) Catalyst: A Functional Model System of Oxidases and Esterases
title: One copper complex, five enzymes' worth of chemistry
blurb: A small-molecule monocopper(II) catalyst mimics five different oxidase and esterase enzymes at once, and the most promiscuous variant, Cu(L-NMe2)2(ClO4)2, owes that range to second-coordination-sphere effects on geometry, redox behavior, and O2 activation. A model system for probing what drives the promiscuity, not a working enzyme replacement.

original_title: A Novel Trigonal Prismatic Rhenium Complex of 2-Hydroxythiobenzhydrazide as a Potent and Selective Anticancer Agent
title: A rhenium complex trying to do platinum's job without platinum's toxicity
blurb: A series of thiohydrazide rhenium complexes aimed at the toxicity and resistance problems that plague platinum chemo. The lead compound, Re[HL2]3, adopts an unusual trigonal-prismatic geometry that tracks with stronger cytotoxic activity, and it's selective for cancer cells over normal ones in the reported data, the standard early promise for a would-be platinum alternative.

original_title: Activating Hard Lewis Acid Cr Sites via Electron Pumps for Enhancing the HMFOR Electrochemical–Chemical Cascade on Ni(OH)2
title: Sulfur electron pumps make chromium do the heavy lifting in HMF oxidation
blurb: Nickel hydroxide catalysts for the HMF-to-FDCA electro-oxidation cascade are normally starved of the Ni3+ sites the chemical step needs. Wiring in sulfur sites as electron pumps activates otherwise-inert chromium sites instead, and the resulting S,Cr-Ni(OH)2/NF catalyst hits 175 mA/cm2 at 1.45 V with 96.9% Faradaic efficiency to FDCA.

original_title: Glycerol-to-Lactic Acid Conversion on a Pd3Pb Surface via a Faradaic and Non-Faradaic Tandem Catalytic Process
title: Pd3Pb triples lactic acid yield from glycerol waste, and gets there two ways at once
blurb: A Pd3Pb alloy catalyst pushes glycerol oxidation toward lactic acid instead of the usual grab-bag of C3 byproducts, hitting 58.3% LA selectivity at 0.65 V vs RHE in alkaline media, up from roughly 20% on plain Pd (87.4% total C3 selectivity). The more interesting bit is mechanistic: the reaction runs through both a Faradaic and a non-Faradaic pathway in tandem, which is exactly the ambiguity this field has been arguing over.

original_title: Fluorescently labeled Angiopep-2-conjugated-PAMAM nanoparticles to evaluate drug brain-targeted delivery performance.
title: Fluorescent tagging to check if Angiopep-2 nanoparticles actually reach the brain
blurb: PAMAM dendrimer nanoparticles conjugated to the brain-targeting peptide Angiopep-2, with a fluorescent tag added so delivery to brain tissue can actually be measured instead of assumed.

original_title: Biomimetic Core–Shell Liposome Nanoparticles Deplete Lipoproteins and Enhance the Purity of Extracellular Vesicles from Human Blood
title: Scrubbing lipoproteins out of blood so extracellular vesicle prep isn't contaminated junk
blurb: Serum EVs are a pain to isolate cleanly because lipoproteins sit at nearly the same size and density, and existing depletion methods miss some of them or add contamination of their own. This system uses Fe3O4@SiO2 cores wrapped in a liposome shell that mimics the lipoprotein surface to pull them out selectively, leaving a purer EV sample for whatever biomarker work comes next.

original_title: Single-Atom Defects Break the Trade-Off Between Intrinsic Activity and Site Density on Fe for Ammonia Synthesis
title: Ammonia catalysts get better by waking up the 'inert' terrace atoms
blurb: Ammonia catalysis has always been about the rare, low-coordinated step sites, while the abundant flat terrace atoms just sit there as spectators. This finds an inverse relationship between activity and surface coordination across different Fe facets, then engineers low-coordination defects directly into the terrace, adding active sites without giving up intrinsic activity, on the actual industrial Fe catalyst rather than a model surface.

original_title: Chain-Growth Synthesis of Sequence-Defined Native Polypeptides via Traceless Cascade Polymerization
title: A chain-growth method for building native polypeptides
blurb: Synthetic polymer chemistry and nature's sequence-defined polymers have mostly evolved on separate tracks. This applies chain-growth polymerization to native polypeptides instead of synthetic monomers, using a traceless peri-naphthalene group to relay the propagating chain end while stitching peptide segments together, then clearing out, hence the name.

original_title: Lower-temperature bulk depolymerization of commercial polymethacrylates
title: PMMA-type plastics finally depolymerize without needing a bespoke design
blurb: Chemical recycling of these polymers has mostly needed thermally fragile custom materials or heavily diluted conditions to work at all. This runs a bulk main-chain scission that depolymerizes commercial polymethacrylates at low temperature in high yield, no preinstalled end-groups or sacrificial comonomers required, so it works on the plastic already in circulation rather than a specially engineered recyclable version of it.

original_title: Low-Temperature Thermal Depolymerization of Polymethacrylates
title: Recycling PMMA at 170°C with peroxides instead of 450°C pyrolysis
blurb: Standard PMMA recycling means pyrolysis above 450°C or photochemistry limited by how deep light can penetrate. This swaps in a purely thermal route at 170°C using off-the-shelf peroxides, and the trick is keeping the radical concentration low enough that oligomers never form, since that's usually what eats into monomer yield. Result: over 95% monomer recovered from native, unmodified PMMA.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: A 3D-printed extraction device based on aptamer-functionalized metal–organic frameworks for ochratoxin A determination in alcoholic beverages
title: A 3D-printed aptamer-MOF cartridge for pulling a mycotoxin out of your drink
blurb: Ochratoxin A extraction from alcoholic beverages, done with an aptamer immobilized on a metal-organic framework and printed into an extraction device. They screened several MOFs under dispersive solid-phase extraction first and landed on UiO-66-(COOH)2 because it barely binds OTA nonspecifically, so the signal is actually coming from the aptamer recognizing its target rather than the MOF just soaking up everything.

original_title: Sono- and Mechanochemical Tandem Synthesis of Diversely Functionalized 1,2,4-Thiadiazoles: A Robust and Straightforward Dual Synthetic Approach
title: Sonochemistry and mechanochemistry team up to build thiadiazoles
blurb: A tandem route to N-fused 1,2,4-thiadiazoles and 5-amino-1,2,4-thiadiazoles from pyridine-2-amines or benzimidamides plus phenyl isothiocyanates, using NIS to drive a dehydrogenative C–N coupling followed by an intramolecular S–N cyclization. Sold as robust and environmentally benign, and getting there through two different tandem mechanisms is a reasonable way to show it's not a fluke of one setup.

original_title: Depth-Resolved Redox Heterogeneity in Inverse CeO2/CuO Catalysts for N2O Decomposition
title: How deep the redox action actually goes in inverse CeO2/CuO catalysts
blurb: N2O decomposition runs on redox cycling, but how far into the catalyst that cycling actually extends during operation was unclear. Depth-resolved X-ray spectroscopy on inverse CeO2/CuO architectures, comparing a normal 20 wt% CuO/CeO2 against an inverted 90 wt% CuO shell made two different ways (flame spray pyrolysis and coprecipitation), maps out the active redox motif and the oxygen-exchange zone that actually sustains turnover.

original_title: Ultra-Tough Hybrid Supramolecular Gelatin Hydrogels.
title: Gelatin hydrogels built to stop tearing
blurb: A hybrid supramolecular crosslinking approach aimed at making gelatin hydrogels genuinely tough instead of the usual soft, fragile gel network.

original_title: Beyond Zolbetuximab: Next-Generation Targeting Strategies for CLDN18.2.
title: What comes after zolbetuximab for CLDN18.2
blurb: A review of next-generation strategies for targeting CLDN18.2, the antigen zolbetuximab made its name on as the first approved antibody against it in GI cancers.

original_title: Real-Time and Rapid Fibrinolysis Analysis Based on Fibrin-Loaded Tubular SiO2–TiO2 Hybrid Inverse Opal
title: A tubular inverse opal that watches clots dissolve in real time
blurb: Fibrin loaded onto a sol-gel grown SiO2-TiO2 tubular inverse opal scaffold, read out by ordered porous layer interferometry, gives a real-time fibrinolysis readout. The scaffold's job is just packing in more fibrin than flat surfaces can, for faster calls on thrombosis or bleeding risk.

original_title: Mechanochemical Control of Stereospecific Strain Release in Chiral Spiroaziridine Oxindoles with Alkyl Amines
title: Ball milling instead of solvent for chiral spiroaziridine ring-opening
blurb: A solvent- and catalyst-free mechanochemical amination opens chiral spiroaziridine oxindoles with alkyl amines, giving 3-aminomethyl-3-alkylamino oxindoles in excellent yields with near-complete transfer of chirality. The actual finding is that grinding preserves stereochemical fidelity better than solution-phase does, mechanical force doing something the solvent apparently can't.

original_title: Two-Point Calibration Surface Plasmon Resonance Immunoassay Enabled by Hadamard-Encoded Spectral Reconstruction and Deep Learning
title: SPR immunoassay drops multipoint calibration for two points and a neural net
blurb: Hadamard-encoded spectral compressive reconstruction paired with a lightweight 1D CNN turns chip-scale nonuniformity, normally something to calibrate away, into free training data, pulling roughly 20,000 pixel-wise training spectra out of a single measurement cycle. The point is getting SPR imaging off laborious multipoint calibration and onto disposable, point-of-care chips.
